description: 2nd connection. 1st connection's RUNSQL failed with a real, useful finding: 'Named argument DATABASE_FILE_TYPE for routine GENERATE_SQL not valid for reason code 1' - GENERATE_SQL accepted DATABASE_OBJECT_NAME/DATABASE_OBJECT_LIBRARY_NAME/DATABASE_SOURCE_FILE_NAME/DATABASE_OBJECT_TYPE/CREATE_OR_REPLACE_OPTION without complaint, only DATABASE_FILE_TYPE was rejected - removed. Second, separate bug in THIS manifest itself (not GENERATE_SQL): GENSQL's own cmd had RUNSQL followed by DSPFD with only a single trailing MONMSG, which (per verify/README.md's own newly-documented trap - MONMSG only guards the immediately preceding command) only covered DSPFD, not RUNSQL - so RUNSQL's own SQL9010 escape went completely unmonitored, causing a Function check that skipped straight past this connection's own FAILSAFE label's graceful handling (no DSPFD output at all appeared in the run section) rather than being caught and reported normally. Fixed by adding an explicit MONMSG immediately after RUNSQL. design doc's own §9 states GENERATE_SQL/RCDFMT have ZERO real primary-source documentation anywhere in work/design/refs/ (only permission-matrix passing mentions) - this connection is still exploratory, testing only whether GENERATE_SQL itself succeeds and what it actually produces (via DSPFD TYPE(*MBRLIST) on the QTEMP source file it should have populated), before attempting the full 'recreate TOKUIM as SQL in QTEMP, compare DSPFD TYPE(*RCDFMT) level IDs against the original' mechanism (this lesson's own core point, B2-17) in a later connection.

steps.label: GENSQL
steps.cmd:
RUNSQL SQL('CALL QSYS2.GENERATE_SQL(DATABASE_OBJECT_NAME => ''TOKUIM'', DATABASE_OBJECT_LIBRARY_NAME => ''&LIB'', DATABASE_SOURCE_FILE_NAME => ''QTEMP/QSQLTEMP'', DATABASE_OBJECT_TYPE => ''*FILE'', CREATE_OR_REPLACE_OPTION => ''1'')') COMMIT(*NONE)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000 SQL0000) EXEC(GOTO CMDLBL(ORIGLVLID))
DSPFD FILE(QTEMP/QSQLTEMP) TYPE(*MBRLIST) OUTPUT(*PRINT)
